item.title: PNG Indonesia international land border to host small business trade fair
item.description: No man's land at Wutung International land border seperating Papua New Guinea and Indonesia will connect both nations through the Border Trade Fair, starting Thursday. The three days event is organized by Provincial Government of Papua in Indonesia and around 66 micro, small and medium enterprises from both nations will be setting up booths to talk commerce and find new business links.
item.content:encoded:
No man's land at Wutung International land border seperating Papua New Guinea and Indonesia will connect both nations through the Border Trade Fair, starting Thursday.

The three days event is organized by Provincial Government of Papua in Indonesia and around 66 micro, small and medium enterprises from both nations will be setting up booths to talk commerce and find new business links.

Papua New Guinea can take a page out of the success book of the Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises to the economy of its giant neighbour - Indonesia.

The MSMEs employs around 97 percent of the workforce in the fourth most populous country in the world.

The Border Trade Fair will run from October 8 to 10 between commonly referred to as "no men's land" the international land crossing from Wutung in West Sepik to Skouw in the Papua Province of Indonesia.

According to Jayapura Customs and Excise Office, export volume to PNG through the international land border is over K12 Million.

And the Border Trade Fair will be an opportunity for PNG Government to start moving the talks from Waigani to Vanimo to increase trade export to the massive economy of the country it shares the only land border with.

Papua Provincial Government of Indonesia and the Indonesian Embassy in a statement stated that, "The Border Trade Fair aims to strengthen corporation between the Republic of Indonesia and the Independent State of Papua New Guinea, particularly in the areas of cross-border trade, local economic development, investment, tourism, community empowerment, and people-to-people relations.

And further read "Indonesian entrepreneur can provide practical example of how to compose local products into attractive, competitive and marketable goods. At the same time, PNG SMEs can share their own traditional products, skills, and knowledge, creating a two-way exchange that can strengthen entrepreneurship and economic cooperation between Papua New Guinea and Indonesia."

item.title: Hailstorm batters food gardens in Enga
item.description: A heavy hailstorm has damaged food gardens and vegetation across four wards in Pilikambi LLG, Laiagam District, Enga Province. The hailstorm struck on Tuesday afternoon, affecting Tupagoos Ward 3, Landelam Ward 7, Kepelam Ward 11 and parts of Kailyam Ward 6.
item.content:encoded:
A heavy hailstorm has damaged food gardens and vegetation across four wards in Pilikambi LLG, Laiagam District, Enga Province.

The hailstorm struck on Tuesday afternoon, affecting Tupagoos Ward 3, Landelam Ward 7, Kepelam Ward 11 and parts of Kailyam Ward 6.

Tupagoos, Landelam and Kepelam were severely affected, with food crops and surrounding vegetation damaged. Similar damage was reported in parts of Kailyam.

The hailstorm is the latest hazard to hit Pilikambi, following an ongoing dry spell linked to El Niño and frost that affected the area in August.

NBC News accompanied the Provincial Disaster Management Office and relevant authorities to the affected areas and witnessed extensive damage to food gardens, which are the main source of food for most households.

The hailstorm snapped sweet potato vines, damaged cabbage patches and stripped leaves from trees and other vegetation.

The storm was described by locals as the heaviest experienced in the area. When NBC News arrived on Wednesday morning, chunks of unmelted ice were still scattered across some areas.

Much of the ice seen in pictures circulating on social media had already melted into the soil by the time of the visit, leaving damaged gardens behind.

Local resident Alas Lou told NBC News the impact on food crops could be serious.

Standing in a two-month-old sweet potato garden badly damaged by the storm, Mr Lou said "crops such as cabbage and potatoes grow well in Pilikambi because of its cold climate".

He said sweet potato is also a staple food, but takes much longer to mature because of the cold conditions.

The hailstorm destroyed newly sprouted sweet potato vines and other crops planted after the frost in August, making it difficult for families who depend on their gardens for food.

Leaders from the affected communities are now calling for urgent relief assistance.

Landelam Ward 7 Councillor Rex Taio, speaking on behalf of his people, said authorities did not provide the necessary relief assistance after the frost hit Pilikambi in August.

He said immediate assistance was needed to prevent a similar situation, as communities rely heavily on their gardens for daily food.

item.title: 20 factory made guns surrendered in Koroba Lake Kopiago District
item.description: Four communities in Koroba–Lake Kopiago District, Hela Province, have voluntarily surrendered 20 factory-made firearms, more than 50 homemade guns, a hand grenade and various traditional weapons, including bows and arrows. The surrender took place on Wednesday and brought together people from Egele, Yaluba 1, Yaluba 2 and Pupa.
item.content:encoded:
Four communities in Koroba–Lake Kopiago District, Hela Province, have voluntarily surrendered 20 factory-made firearms, more than 50 homemade guns, a hand grenade and various traditional weapons, including bows and arrows.

The surrender took place on Wednesday and brought together people from Egele, Yaluba 1, Yaluba 2 and Pupa.

It is the first gun surrender program conducted in Koroba–Lake Kopiago District and the fifth peace ceremony of its kind in Hela Province.

The ceremony was witnessed by Hela Governor Philip Undialu, Koroba–Lake Kopiago MP William Bando, Provincial Administrator Ronny Angu and Provincial Police Commander Inspector Arau Mairi.

Members of the police, PNG Defence Force and local community leaders also attended.

Governor Undialu, who leads the Hela Provincial Gun Surrender Program, commended ward councillors, leaders and community members for their efforts to end years of tribal violence and rebuild peace in their communities.

“We will continue this program throughout Hela until illegal firearms no longer pose a threat to our communities. These foreign weapons have warped minds, turning brother against brother and destroying our villages. Working together, we will restore Hela Province to a place of safety where people can travel freely and access vital services once again,” Governor Undialu said.

Mr Bando said the Yaluba event marks the beginning of a broader district-wide disarmament drive, commending local clans for taking what he described as a decisive step towards lasting peace.

“This marks the beginning of our mission to clear weapons from our district. We urge neighbouring communities to prepare, as our team will move village by village until every tribe and clan surrenders their arms.

“We are doing this for the future of our children and our youth, many of whom have been denied an education due to endless tribal conflict,” Mr Bando said.

He said genuine peace was essential for the delivery of government infrastructure and social services.

The Hela Provincial Gun Surrender Program continues across the district, with neighbouring villages in the Pureni community scheduled to surrender their weapons today.

item.title: Enga disaster office assesses hailstorm damage in Pilikambi
item.description: The Enga Provincial Disaster Office has visited Pilikambi to assess the hailstorm damage, with further household surveys and data collection planned in the coming days. A team from the Disaster Office, DPI office, GESI, Climate Change Office and Community Development office from the provincial government went to the hailstorm affected sites in Pilikambi the next day to view the extent of the damag
item.content:encoded:
The Enga Provincial Disaster Office has visited Pilikambi to assess the hailstorm damage, with further household surveys and data collection planned in the coming days.

A team from the Disaster Office, DPI office, GESI, Climate Change Office and Community Development office from the provincial government went to the hailstorm affected sites in Pilikambi the next day to view the extent of the damage caused and establish communication.

“What we actually did today was that we’ve achieved was that we’ve established communication network.

“Probably tomorrow and the next day we'll be going over there, we’ve established the coordination mechanism already so what we basically so what we basically will be doing tomorrow is getting back to the area to do household surveys and collecting more data,” said Ignas Nembo the On-site Disaster Coordinator with the Enga Disaster Management Office after the trip to Pilikambi.

When questioned about the coordination of relief supplies to the affected communities Mr. Nembo said the Provincial Disaster Office is assisting the District Development Authority to conduct proper survey and produce necessary data reports so the Laiagam DDA can correctly supply relief to the four hailstorm affected Wards.

He said 2.5 million kina has been given to respective DDA’s in the country to cater to El Nino disasters and for Pilikambi’s situation the Laiagam DDA will be funding the relief supply.

item.content:encoded:
On Tuesday afternoon parts of the Pilikambi LLG of the Laiagam district of Enga province experienced one of the heaviest hailstorm in the area and the aftermath of the storm left food gardens and surrounding vegetation in destruction.

Four wards in the Pilikambi LLG of the Laiagam district have been affected by the hailstorm; Tupagoos Ward three, Landelam ward seven and Kepelam ward eleven were severely affected with food crops and surrounding vegetation damaged while parts of Kailyam ward six that experienced the hailstorm sustained similar damage.

This hailstorm follows two prior hazards that had affected Pilikambi over the months; the ongoing dry spell caused by the El Nino that is being experienced through-out the country and frost in August.

NBC News accompanying the provincial disaster management office along with relevant-authorities to the affected sites witnessed the severe damage by the hailstorm on gardens, the main source of food supply for most of the households.

The hailstorm snapped off the tops of crops like sweet potato vines, cabbage patches and stripped leaves from trees and surrounding vegetation.

The hailstorm being the heaviest experienced in the area there was still un-melted ice packed together forming chucks of ice when NBC arrived on seen the next day around eleven o clock.

Most of the ice spread throughout the area showcasing a blanket of snow initially in pictures circulating social media had melted into the soil leaving behind a scene of wreckage.

Alas Lou a local from Ward Seven spoke to NBC on the Impact of the storm on food crops.

Standing in the middle of a two-month-old sweet potato garden that had been battered by the storm Alas said due to the cold climate in Pilikambi a numbered crops grow very well like cabbages and potatoes.

Sweet potato is a staple food as well however, it takes up to a year and five to six months to mature due to the cold climate of the area.

The hailstorm has destroyed the newly sprouted sweet potato vines as well as other food crops that were planted after the frost bite back in August making it harder for families to cater for themselves.

Leaders from the affected areas are calling on authorities to provide relief supplies immediately.

Councilor of Landelam Ward Seven Rex Taio on behalf of his people said when frost hit Pilikambi in August authorities did not provide necessary relief assistance to his people. To avoid this similar situation, he says rapid relief assistance is necessary as people depend on gardens for daily survival.

item.title: WSPHA maintain operation despite dry spell
item.description: The West Sepik Provincial Health Authority (WSPHA) is continuing its full operations despite the prolonged dry season affecting the province and other parts of the country. While several schools and health centers nationwide have scaled down operations due to water shortages, WSPHA Chief Executive Officer Stanley Masi says Vanimo General Hospital is not affected.
item.content:encoded:
The West Sepik Provincial Health Authority (WSPHA) is continuing its full operations despite the prolonged dry season affecting the province and other parts of the country.

While several schools and health centers nationwide have scaled down operations due to water shortages, WSPHA Chief Executive Officer Stanley Masi says Vanimo General Hospital is not affected.

Mr. Masi told NBC News the hospital has a water bore well source that supplies water for toilets, laundry and general cleaning, while rainwater tanks are used for drinking water for both patients and staff.

Meanwhile, CEO Masi confirmed the Authority is yet to receive any El Nino funding from the National Department of Health, the National Government or the Sandaun Provincial Government to support rural health facilities.

"For us in Vanimo, the hospital is doing fine. Our main concern is Telefomin, which is now experiencing severe drought and water shortage. Other centers affected, include Nuku, Aitape and Lumi who are now scaling down on some of its services," Mr. Masi said.

The National Government has released El Nino funds to provincial and district administrations to support essential services like health and education, Mr. Masi hopes the PHA will receive a portion to support its district hospitals and health centers.

Mr. Masi added that it is time the National Government funds PHAs directly, rather than channeling funds through the National Department of Health.

item.title: Assembly calls for proper reporting
item.description: ‎Divisional and Departmental heads within the Milne Bay Provincial Administration in Milne Bay Province, have been urged to provide timely reports on major activities in the province. ‎ ‎This call was made by Acting Chairman and Deputy Governor, Mathew Magioudi, during the province's assembly meeting on Friday following concerns over the lack of activity reports from some government divisions. ‎ ‎
item.content:encoded:
‎Divisional and Departmental heads within the Milne Bay Provincial Administration in Milne Bay Province, have been urged to provide timely reports on major activities in the province. ‎ ‎This call was made by Acting Chairman and Deputy Governor, Mathew Magioudi, during the province's assembly meeting on Friday following concerns over the lack of activity reports from some government divisions. ‎ ‎During a session of questions without notice, a supplementary question was raised in the assembly regarding Timber and logging operations in the province, including it's licenses and permits, the benefits they are bringing to the people of Milne Bay.

However, no detailed report was presented as Chairman responsible for forestry did not have any report at hand to answer the series of questions. ‎ ‎This prompted the Acting Chairman and Deputy Governor, Mathew Magioudi, who sternly called on the Provincial Administration to immediately look into addressing the failure by some departmental and divisional heads in providing accurate and detailed reports to respective chairmen in the Provincial Assembly. ‎ ‎"It is very frustrating to see that the divisional heads and certain department managers have not been working together with their chairman's. Non-compliant to PEC and assembly requirements are very bad", The acting Chairman said ‎ ‎"I wish to call upon and put on record in this assembly; the administrator of various departments responsible must take seriously the concerns and the welfare of the people of Milne Bay Province" ‎ ‎The acting Chairman advised the provincial administration that the Assembly is the only forum through which the public gets to hear and learn about what the government is doing for them as other communication mediums are not effective in remote areas. ‎ ‎He stressed that proper and timely reporting is therefore very essential for accountability and transparency, adding that a lack of accurate information from divisional and departmental heads makes it difficult for the provincial assembly to effectively scrutinize government activities, funded programs and the impact it has on communities.

‎He added that respective advisors in the provincial administration must understand that providing reports is part of their responsibility to the Provincial Government and the general public.
